info.title: pixverse/v6
info.description: The request body Comfy Router accepts for the model "pixverse/v6", and the response body it returns. The INPUT schema is the same schema the server validates a call against before it reaches the provider, so what is published and what is enforced cannot differ. `x-comfy-router-input-modalities` records the media kinds the model is documented to accept; the request schema is shared across sibling models and may admit media kinds this model ignores. The OUTPUT schema describes the provider's native result document exactly as Router returns it: Router does not validate, narrow or re-envelope the response, so the output schema is descriptive rather than enforced, and Comfy owns no output shape of its own.

schema.description:
The PixVerse text-to-video fields, shared by the v1 `POST /proxy/pixverse/video/text/generate` request body and the Comfy Router input schema for `pixverse/v3.5`, `pixverse/v6` and `pixverse/v6-max`. See the note above `RecraftImageGenerationInputs` for why the two surfaces share properties but not `required`.
`required` here is the ROUTER-SAFE floor: `model` is absent from it because Router writes the path's model into the body after routervalidate.Guard has already validated the caller's bytes. The v1 wrapper `PixverseTextVideoRequest` re-adds it.

example.prompt: a single red maple leaf falling onto still water

model.description: PixVerse text-to-video model identifier. On the Comfy Router route `POST /v2/models/pixverse/{model}` this field is supplied from the path and may be omitted.

200.description: OK - the model's native JSON output, returned unchanged; the schema describes the provider's terminal result document as Router returns it.

schema.description:
Comfy Router output schema for the PixVerse text-to-video models: the partner's own result document, forwarded once Router has polled to a terminal success. The operation is submit-and-poll (`routerresult/classification.go` classifies POST /proxy/pixverse/video/text/generate as ReturnModeSubmitPoll, polled on GET /video/result/:id), so the body a caller receives is this finished document, not the submit's video_id handle.
A terminal success has Resp.status 1 and a non-empty Resp.url, which is the output video. The Router poll family requires that URL; a status-1 document with no URL is treated as a success with no output rather than handed back as a finished video. Billing quantities (`Resp.credits`) are reported only after the run, which is why Quote answers ok=false.
